title.narrative: Targeted communities and parents are able to advocate for the right to education for children with developmental disabilities to increase their access to primary education

description.narrative: Both AfA and IDA will work at community level to form SelfHelp Groups (SHGs) of parents of children with developmental disabilities. HI has experience in forming and supporting SHGs that have good governance, clear roles, responsibilities and financial procedures and this learning will be transferred to AfA and IDA. The SHGs capacity will be enhanced so that they are empowered to advocate and raise awareness of the right to education for their children with developmental disabilities.The parents SHGs will play a crucial role in raising awareness in their local communities about the right to education for their children with developmental disabilities. The SHGs will also be supported to develop and plan for advocacy activities at the DESB and PESS levels.

title.narrative: Output 1. Two Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) Association for Autism (AfA) and Intellectual Disability Association (IDA) have the capacity to increase access to education for children with developmental disabilities by working at community level

description.narrative: Following the European Commissions description , this action takes the definition of CSOs as organizations that are nonstate, notforprofit, and nonviolent through which people organize to pursue shared objectives and ideals, whether political, cultural, social or economic. AfA and IDA are the only two CSOs in Lao PDR who provide access to education for children with developmental disabilities. AfA was established and registered in 2012 as a Parent Support Network in Vientiane. AfA has 72 members from different provinces of Lao PDR and a branch in Champasak Province. AfA operates two autism centers, one in Vientiane and another in Pakse (Champasak Province). Pakse autism center was established in 2017 with strong support from HI. AfA has a dynamic director and a very proactive board, with support of financial and personnel resources they can expand to other provinces. While IDA only received NonProfit Association (NPA) status in 2018, HI supported IDA through a previous EU grant to develop their Strategic Action Plan in 2018 which can only be implemented if they have resources and coaching. HI will also support AfA and IDA to develop skills in the use of the Washington Group Child Functioning Module to identify functional limitations of children as well as learn from their Early Childhood Development project and enable them to develop local pathways for multidisciplinary health assessments and diagnosis in Champasak and Huaphan. HI will also support IDA to improve its governance to meet Lao laws. SOSIE will also build in resources for purchase of assistive devices and communication aids to improve childrens learning outcomes.

AfA was established and registered in 2012 as a Parent Support Network in Vientiane. AfA has 72 members from different provinces of Lao PDR and a branch in Champasak Province. AfA operates two autism centers, one in Vientiane and another in Pakse (Champasak Province). Pakse autism center was established in 2017 with strong support from HI. AfA has a dynamic director and a very proactive board, with support of financial and personnel resources they can expand to other provinces. While IDA only received NonProfit Association (NPA) status in 2018, HI supported IDA through a previous EU grant to develop their Strategic Action Plan in 2018 which can only be implemented if they have resources and coaching. HI will also support AfA and IDA to develop skills in the use of the Washington Group Child Functioning Module to identify functional limitations of children as well as learn from their Early Childhood Development project and enable them to develop local pathways for multidisciplinary health assessments and diagnosis in Champasak and Huaphan. HI will also support IDA to improve its governance to meet Lao laws. SOSIE will also build in resources for purchase of assistive devices and communication aids to improve childrens learning outcomes.

title.narrative: To contribute to improving access to quality inclusive education for the most marginalized children in Laos PDR.

description.narrative: The overall objective is to contribute to improving access to quality inclusive education for the most marginalized children in Lao PDR.Through a global empowerment and cooperation of vulnerable groups, CSOs, Local Authorities, the project is fully aligned with: UN Sustainable Development Goal (SGDs): SDG 4 (Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all).Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD): Article 7 (Children with disabilities), Article 24 (Education).EU Disability Strategy 20102020: EU priority area 5 on Education and training (promote inclusive education and lifelong learning for students and pupils with disabilities. Equal access to quality education and lifelong learning enable disabled people to participate fully in society and improve their quality of life).Lao PDR National Law on Disability: Decree on Persons with Disabilities.The action will contribute to the overall objective by achieving the specific objective of a reinforcement of the capacity of Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), Educators, Provincial Education and Sports Service (PESS) and District of Education and Sports Bureau (DESB) to enable access to quality inclusive primary education in Champasak and Huaphan provinces for the most marginalized children through the support of communities and parents.

Equal access to quality education and lifelong learning enable disabled people to participate fully in society and improve their quality of life).Lao PDR National Law on Disability: Decree on Persons with Disabilities.The action will contribute to the overall objective by achieving the specific objective of a reinforcement of the capacity of Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), Educators, Provincial Education and Sports Service (PESS) and District of Education and Sports Bureau (DESB) to enable access to quality inclusive primary education in Champasak and Huaphan provinces for the most marginalized children through the support of communities and parents.
